description: A differential heuristic estimates distances from exact distances to and from a few chosen states, the *landmarks*. For a landmark `L` and a goal `g`, the triangle inequality gives `d(v, g) ≥ d(L, g) − d(L, v)` and `d(v, g) ≥ d(v, L) − d(g, L)`; the heuristic takes the largest of these bounds over all landmarks, and at least zero. The crate does this for each objective on its own, with two Dijkstra searches per landmark and objective, and returns the vector of bounds. The estimate never overestimates, and it is consistent along every edge whose end can reach the goal, so exact multi-objective searches stay exact. Use it on a large, fixed graph that gets many queries to different goals.
